clue.text: Men bowled over by fine bird …

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked flat and turned upside down, so in this down clue the word for men is read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A batsman's dismissal seems to be watched by a splendid bird, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the forces' term for ordinary soldiers; 'bowled over' in a down clue means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a black crow-family bird, and also a chess piece, fitting the puzzle's chess theme.

clue.text: … and more court daughter with slow dancing

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move around, so the word slow is rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing from the bird, a suitor courts a daughter by dancing slowly with her.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis makes 'more' mean more birds, following the previous clue's bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood owls are a group of owls, so they are further examples of birds after the previous clue's rook.

clue.text: College in Cambridge or in New York?

definitions.meaning: ...' College is one of the colleges of Cambridge University
... is one of the five boroughs of New York City, so something there is in ...

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether the institution is in the English university town or the American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge, Massachusetts tempts one to look across the Atlantic for the college; the American half is really the New York borough.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves a Cambridge college and a borough of New York City, and queens are also chess pieces.

clue.text: Number it: a 100 written up as symbols

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing something up means setting it out from the bottom upwards, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a number down as figures and symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns the whole string NO IT A TON upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Notation is a system of written signs, as in musical or chess notation, so it is a set of symbols.

clue.text: Champion in utter darkness

indicators.note: to utter is to say out loud, so the word for darkness is spoken and the spelling heard is entered

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: A hero languishes in complete blackness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like the adjective meaning complete; it is the verb, to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight was a champion who fought on behalf of a lord or lady; the knight is also a chess piece.

clue.text: Nails cut up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so the synonym for cut is reversed

parts.note: to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: Fingernails are trimmed back.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something in place is to pin or fasten it, so the verb nails matches pins.

clue.text: 10001000 teachers might be kind of shy

parts.note: split as 100, 0, 100, 0: C is the Roman numeral for 100 and O looks like zero
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teachers' union

explanation.surface: A string of digits that teachers might find a little bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: The digits read 100-0-100-0. A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock coconuts off posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A coconut shy is a type of fairground throwing game, so coconut names a kind of shy.

clue.text: Labour employs leading economist over article for growth

indicators.note: a firm that employs people takes them in, so the word for labour holds the other pieces

parts.note: toil is hard labour

indicators.note: the leading letter of economist is its first
turned over means read backwards, so the article is reversed

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The Labour Party hires a senior economist to write an article about economic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' reads as the political party but is plain hard work; 'over' reverses the article before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A toenail is a horny growth at the tip of a toe.

clue.text: Small child's slide?

parts.note: a kid is a child; the 's is read as has, so the small letter has the kid with it

explanation.surface: A question whether this is a slide meant for a little one in a playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is an uncontrolled sliding movement, as of a car on ice.

clue.text: Old church's financial backers lose pound sterling in trades

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: the backers lose something, so a letter is taken out of their word

parts.note: angels are people who put money into a theatrical production
L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: An old church's donors lose their money in bad deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' takes L out of ANGELS, leaving ANGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanges are swaps of one thing for another, the same as trades.

clue.text: Former party leader inherits real mess and can be excused

indicators.note: someone who inherits takes something in, so the leader's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Sir Vince Cable was leader of the Liberal Democrats, a British party, from 2017 to 2019

indicators.note: making a mess of letters jumbles them, so real is rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-leader takes over a real shambles from a predecessor and is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former party leader' is not any former leader but specifically Vince Cable of the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clearable can be cleared, as a person can be cleared of blame or excused.

clue.text: Break back carrying wife's deposits as security

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it, so the reversed word for break holds the letter for wife
going back means read backwards, so the synonym for break is reversed

parts.note: to snap is to break
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man with a broken back takes his wife's savings to the moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SNAP into PANS, which carries W.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn something is to leave it with a lender as security for a loan; pawns are also chess pieces.

clue.text: A little bit of quiet on the radio

indicators.note: words on the radio are heard rather than read, so the word for quiet is taken by its sound

parts.note: peace is quiet or calm

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a moment of silence on the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a small part or portion of something; a chessman is also called a piece.

clue.text: They send out Mister Messy to collect note

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so the jumbled letters hold the note
a messy arrangement is disordered, so the letters of mister are rearranged

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A man named Mister Messy, like a children's book character, is sent out to collect a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messy' scrambles MISTER into EMITRS, and the note goes in after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Emitters are things that give out light, sound or signals, so they send out.

clue.text: Even reversing, I would be quick

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word for even is read the other way

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone claims that even when driving in reverse they would be fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns PAR into RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid is a direct synonym of quick or fast.

clue.text: In the end policies bore, admit focus groups

indicators.note: the end of each of the four words supplies a letter, taken from the tail of each

explanation.surface: Voters in focus groups finally admit that the policies are boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets are collections of people or things belonging together, just as groups are.

clue.text: Partners suppress anger with alarm

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so the partners' letters enclose the anger

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as partners, abbreviated N and S
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A couple try to keep their temper in check when the alarm sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge pairs North and South as partners, giving S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a device sounding a loud warning, so it is an alarm.

clue.text: It's beautiful out

definitions.meaning: workers who are out are on strike

explanation.surface: Someone admires how lovely the weather is outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking can describe impressive good looks, and also workers who have walked out in a dispute.

clue.text: Remove stolen contents

indicators.note: the contents of a word are what lies inside it, so its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: swiped is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: An order to clear away loot that has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' keeps the inside of SWIPED, losing S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something away is to remove it, as to wipe a mark off a table.

clue.text: Arguments with scientists about fish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scientists' letters go round the fishing word

parts.note: RS, the Royal Society, is Britain's academy of scientists
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Scientists bicker over a species of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is the verb, to angle, not a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrangles are long, noisy disputes, a synonym for arguments.

clue.text: Plant has Ubers manufactured

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A factory has turned out a fleet of Uber taxis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the factory of the surface but is the vegetable sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shrub is a bushy plant growing by the coast, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Hit golf ball badly over river, then withdrew

indicators.note: the golf stroke sits over the river letter, straddling it, so the river goes inside

parts.note: to shank is to mishit a golf ball off the heel of the club

explanation.surface: A golfer mishits a shot over a stream and then retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back is to recoil or withdraw, so shrank matches withdrew.

clue.text: Perhaps Shakespeare eats no meals

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside, so the poet's title holds the letter

parts.note: Shakespeare is the Bard, an example of a bard or poet
O is zero, nothing, so it can stand for no

explanation.surface: The playwright goes without his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' as O, the figure nought, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Board means the meals provided, as in bed and board.

clue.text: Holy man to dance around his building

indicators.note: the dance word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to bop is to dance

indicators.note: building something means assembling it, so the letters of his are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A priest is set to dance round his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' is not a church here but the anagram signal on 'his'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior clergyman, so a holy man; the bishop is also a chess piece.

clue.text: Kept, as are exotic birds

indicators.note: exotic means strange or unusual, so the letters are turned into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: These birds are kept as exotic pets are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' reads as part of the definition, exotic birds, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets are small long-tailed parrots, so they are birds.

clue.text: Dads drink on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits on top of it

parts.note: pop is fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: Fathers have a drink on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Pops is an informal American name for fathers.

clue.text: Cricket, maybe, is mega-excited

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and stirred up, so the letters of mega are stirred

explanation.surface: Cricket is said to be super thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is an example of a game, the bat-and-ball sport; chess is another.

clue.text: Worried to support married couple

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the piece it holds up

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A troubled partner props up a wedded pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' gives ATE, from the sense of something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to pair up or couple, as animals do; mate also ends a chess game.

clue.text: Gap garment a third off — over nine grand!

indicators.note: a third of a three-letter word is one letter, so the first letter of the garment is dropped

parts.note: a top is a garment

indicators.note: turned over means read backwards, so nine is reversed

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A shopper exclaims over a garment with a third off now costing over nine thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third off' cuts T from TOP to leave OP; 'over' turns NINE into ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a gap or aperture; it is also the first moves of a chess game.

clue.text: Something unusual in books about lovesick Yankee

indicators.note: the books' letters go about the jumbled letters

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

indicators.note: something sick is out of sorts, so the letters of love are put out of order

parts.note: Yankee is the radio alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: A lovesick American appears in some books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovesick' looks like one word but splits: 'sick' scrambles LOVE into OVEL, held by NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelty is something new and unusual, a synonym for a curiosity.
